attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the conclusion in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the present-tense observation, expected-return comparison, and majority qualifier. The surrounding discussion establishes generative AI as the subject.

contract.note: Comparing realized financial returns with business customers' expectations is an ordinary reading. The contract reasonably uses current 2025 experience and distinguishes disappointing returns from pending returns or any positive benefit.

evidence.note: Relevant, timely survey evidence, but significant realized ROI is a different metric from meeting expectations. Respondents awaiting returns cannot automatically be counted as disappointed.
The report is timely contextual evidence. Pilot-level financial impact and its limited sample do not establish the share of business customers whose returns fell short of expectations.
Valid contextual evidence about limited business value, but it covers AI broadly and does not compare generative AI returns with customer expectations.

This timely vendor-commissioned disclosure provides positive-return counterevidence. Its deployed-user sample and use-case returns do not establish whether overall customer expectations were met; it is not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: None of the studies measures whether most business customers' realized generative AI returns met their expectations for the same investment and elapsed period. Limited significant returns do not establish disappointment, while positive use-case returns do not establish satisfied expectations. The packet settles neither side.
